newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-"DANCE OF THE COACHES" GATHERS PACE IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-"DANCE OF THE COACHES" GATHERS PACE IN BRAZIL.

text.p: Sao Paulo and Flamengo were both searching for new managers on Tuesday as Brazil's so-called "dance of the coaches" went into full swing.
Muricy Ramalho was relieved of his post at Sao Paulo on Monday for the second time in little more than a year following the 3-3 draw with Guarani at the weekend.
Ramalho had taken over when Carlos Alberto Parreira, who won the World Cup with Brazil in 1994, was dismissed last year.

He had also been given the job in March last year when Tele Santana resigned through ill-health, but was later pushed aside to make way for Parreira, now with the MetroStars in the United States' MLS league.
Former World Cup player Junior, sacked in the wake of Sunday's 1-1 draw at Madureira, became the fifth Flamengo coach to lose his job in since Kleber Leite took over as club president two years ago.
Junior had been under pressure since the club suffered one of its biggest humiliations last month.

Flamengo needed to beat Botafogo to qualify for the final of the first stage of the Rio de Janeiro championship and seemed certain to do so when Botafogo, already through, opted to field a reserve team. Yet Flamengo lost 1-0.
The incessant chopping and changing of coaches in Brazil is nicknamed "the dance of the coaches".
Seven of the 16 clubs in the Sao Paulo championship have changed coaches since it began less than two months ago.

These include Sao Jose and America-Sao Jose do Rio Preto, who are already on to their third manager and Guarani, where president Beto Zini is nicknamed "The Exterminator of the President" because of the number of coaches he sacks. Last year, Zini employed 10 coaches.
Outside the Sao Paulo region, Fluminense, Cruzeiro and Bahia have also changed coaches this year.
Almost as stunning as the club's lack of patience is their cheek at approaching team bosses established at other clubs.

Since dismissing Junior on Monday, reports in Brazil say that Flamengo have approached Luis Felipe Scolari at Japanese club Jubilo Iwota in Japan, Parreira, Vanderley Luxemburgo at Santos and Paulo Autuori at Cruzeiro.
None of the candidates have been at their clubs for more than three months and all were reported to have rejected Flamengo's advances.

After a similar sequence of negative answers in 1995, Flamengo became so desperate they turned to radio commentator Washingon Rodrigues -- a man with absolutely no playing or coaching experience. He lasted nearly four months, which is not bad by Brazilian standards.
Flamengo and Sao Paulo players hinted on Tuesday that they would appreciate more stability.
"Junior was doing a good job but they made him the scapegoat," said Flamengo goalkeeper Ze Carlos, who scored an own goal on Sunday.
Sao Paulo goalkeeper Rogerio commented: "Only the players can change the situation. Muricy was doing everything he could."
